When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10**, calm, WATCH mode with **1** to **2** signals vs VIX Spike Tier **4/4**, EXTREME, **85%** probability, skew plus backwardation plus adaptive all active simultaneously
The Crash Index measures realized price-based stress; the VIX Spike measures forward options structure. Both can be simultaneously true. Trust the VIX Spike here because skew and backwardation firing together is a forward-looking structural read, not a lagging one.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **43/100**, ACCUMULATE partial signal vs Divergence composite in TOPPING zone with **27** of **43** pairs bearish and Mother Jaws at **100/100**
A partial contrarian buy can trigger while divergence is topping if sentiment has deteriorated enough to cross accumulation thresholds while leadership narrows. The divergence picture at a composite score of **100** is the more structural read for sizing. Treat the contrarian signal as a floor, nothing more.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The regime is in TRANSITION at 43/100 with a MIXED bias, and that score earns its ambiguity: you have competing signals that do not resolve into a clean directional call. The VIX Spike is at Tier 4/4 with 85% probability and all three confirming detectors active (skew, backwardation, adaptive), yet the Crash Index sits at 1/10. These two readings describe different markets running at different speeds: the price market is calm and the options market is positioned for vol expansion.

The CONCENTRATION macro regime at 55% confidence tells you where the gains are pooling. NDX at +5.3% over five days versus RUT at -0.8% is the regime expressing itself in real time. You lean into confirmed leaders and stay defensive on breadth-dependent trades, specifically small caps, equal-weight, anything that needs RUT participation to work. The contrarian score at 43 offers a partial accumulation signal, partial being the operative word.

The reading that flips the stance is the Crash Index adding a second signal. One signal in WATCH mode is manageable. Two starts a cascade, especially in a market where the Mother Jaws composite sits at 100 and 69.77% of pairs are already in bearish divergence.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The CONCENTRATION macro regime at 55% confidence describes a market where gains are pooling in a narrow set of leaders rather than spreading across the board. NDX at +5.3% over five days versus RUT at -0.8% is that regime made visible.

At 55% confidence, the call is real but not overwhelming. You position in the leaders, keep small-cap and equal-weight exposure light, and watch whether confidence moves higher (regime entrenching) or reverses toward neutral (regime breaking).

A CONCENTRATION regime that breaks tends to break fast when the leaders crack: the conceptual stop is the point where NDX and RUT start converging from the wrong direction.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence, in plain terms, measures how many asset pairs that historically moved together have stopped doing so. Correlation drift is the size of that breakdown: a pair at +0.79 was moving almost in lockstep; the same pair at -0.34 now moves in opposite directions.

The Mother Jaws composite at 100 (its maximum) with 69.77% of 43 pairs in bearish divergence means the structural underpinning of this rally is narrow. QQQ versus SPY drifted from +0.79 to -0.34: tech is decoupling from the broad market, carrying the index while most stocks fade.

KRE versus XLF drifted from +0.18 to -0.62: regional banks are now moving sharply against the broader financial sector, a stress signal that has not yet shown up in credit spreads. Visa versus Mastercard drifted from +0.66 to -0.70: two near-identical businesses moving in opposite directions signals rotation or idiosyncratic stress inside a sector that looked homogeneous.

USMV versus SPY drifted from -0.92 to +0.09: the low-volatility factor, historically a clean hedge against SPY drawdowns, has lost that relationship entirely, removing a key defensive tool from the toolkit. XBI versus IBB drifted from +0.50 to -0.38: small-cap biotech is breaking away from large-cap biotech.

With 27 bearish and 3 bullish pairs and the composite in a TOPPING zone, most of the market is quietly deteriorating beneath the index level.

AI read · the cross-region tape

KOSPI at +6.8% over five days is the week's strongest print globally, outpacing NDX at +5.3% and every other major index in the data. HSI at +0.7% over the same window shows Asia is split: Korea is running, Hong Kong is barely moving.

Europe is flat to modestly positive, with STOXX50E at +1.0% while the DAX sits at 0.0%. The US confirms the CONCENTRATION read: NDX at +5.3% leading while RUT at -0.8% lags.

In crypto, SOL at +5.7% is outpacing ETH at +2.3%, a high-beta-over-value signal within the asset class. The global tape is selective: gains are accruing in momentum pockets (KOSPI, NDX, SOL) while broader indices are flat or negative.

The KOSPI lead supports risk appetite at the margin for the US session, but the DAX flatline and RUT underperformance confirm the bid is thin outside the leaders.

Forward-looking indicators · Bonferroni-validated
Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

Crash Index at 1/10 and VIX Spike at Tier 4/4 describe two different clocks running at different speeds, and reading them together is the point. The Crash Index counts realized, price-based signals: drawdowns, momentum breaks, spread blowouts.

One signal active means those have not materialized. The VIX Spike reads the forward options structure, specifically whether skew is bid, whether the term structure is in backwardation (near-term vol more expensive than longer-dated), and whether the adaptive threshold has fired.

All three are active today. Options traders are paying up for protection against a move the price market has not yet produced.

That can mean smart hedging ahead of a known catalyst or options markets running ahead of themselves. The Crash Index at 1/10 keeps this in the hedging category until a second realized signal arrives, at which point the two clocks start to agree.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
